rationale: Research product recording a new high-consequence Surface on the accepted map (base version 3) and one new feedback lead. Reading the previously deferred transport surfaces exposed that processHeartbeat is the only entry into appendEntries that skips checkRPCHeader, and that the network transport routes pure heartbeats to it. The product does not fabricate an obligation: the obligation relation is missing because the reachability and consequence premises are unresolved, which is exactly what the Surface and the remaining list state. No existing behavior, fact, requirement or Surface is changed, so accepted obligations and results keep their original basis; the map gains one deferred Surface with its sources.

feedback.answered: New sourced lead on a core path, not an obligation: the appendEntries handler has two entry paths with different guards. raft.go:1390-1413 routes normal RPCs through checkRPCHeader (which enforces the supported protocol-version window) before dispatching AppendEntries, while raft.go:1415-1436 (processHeartbeat, installed as the transport fast path at api.go:616) calls appendEntries directly. net_transport.go:660-686 classifies a pure AppendEntries with Term != 0, a leader address, no entries, PrevLogEntry/PrevLogTerm zero and LeaderCommitIndex zero as a heartbeat and net_transport.go:724-733 hands it to the handler without any header check. On that path appendEntries can still step a receiver down and persist a newer term, adopt the sender as known leader and refresh lastContact.
remaining: Whether a peer whose RPCHeader.ProtocolVersion falls outside the window checkRPCHeader rejects can reach a pure heartbeat to a follower in practice, and whether any consequence follows beyond the version gate itself.

Whether the omission is deliberate (the fast path being understood as a shortcut that assumes already-validated peers) or an unintended asymmetry: no comment on processHeartbeat or on the transport fast path states that the header gate is intentionally skipped.
The confirmed ConfigurationStore delivery violation is settled in scope and needs no further work; the open question there (whether batching FSMs are contractually exempt) stays a limitation.
feedback.rationale: The new Surface preserves a real, sourced asymmetry between two entry paths for the same request type without presuming it is a defect. It is recorded now rather than escalated to a Candidate because the reachability premise (a legal peer sending a heartbeat outside the supported protocol window) and the consequence are both unestablished. The next step is premise investigation: read checkRPCHeader's callers and the transport's version handling to decide whether an attributed obligation is available or whether the asymmetry is intentional design.

surface:processHeartbeat / net_transport.rationale: New high-consequence Surface, not a change to any existing object. It records that the same AppendEntriesRequest shape is subject to two different entry paths: processRPC applies checkRPCHeader before appendEntries, while the heartbeat fast path processHeartbeat reaches appendEntries with no header check, and net_transport routes pure heartbeats to that handler. No behavior, fact, requirement or previously accepted Surface is modified.
